text:
maya: FYI Sable hit a sudden token-per-second spike ~4800 tps on their dedicated pool and started getting 429s from admission control. They say this started after a marketing push. Logs attached below.

liam: can you paste the admission logs and the pool config? also which pool id?

maya: pool=d-sable-4, sending two snippets. first is admission rejects, then autoscaler hints.

maya: ```
[2026-03-16T15:02:14Z] admission: reject req pool=d-sable-4 reason=burst_credits_exhausted headroom=0 tps_window=60s observed=4789 allow_rate=220
[2026-03-16T15:02:15Z] admission: queue_len=128 avg_latency_ms=420
[2026-03-16T15:02:16Z] autoscaler: scale_up requested=6 current_replicas=2 pending=0 cooldown=120s
[2026-03-16T15:02:17Z] runtime: noisy_gpu_detected node=gpu-12 tail_latency_p95=620
```

sophie: looks like burst credits went to zero quickly. did billing or credit accounting show any recent refill events?

diego: ran rcli against their pool just now:
```
$ rcli pool show d-sable-4 --fields=burst_credits,refill_rate,min_replicas,max_replicas
burst_credits: 0
refill_rate: 600_tokens_per_minute
min_replicas: 2
max_replicas: 8
current_replicas: 2
prewarm_enabled: false
```

noah: refill_rate looks low for a sustained multi-k tps spike. also min_replicas=2 means autoscaler had to spin up nodes which takes time; combined with noisy GPU and admission headroom=0 = recipe for 429s.

liam: is this strictly token/tps accounting or did the auth layer also throttle? we saw weird 401s in the earlier window from Sable's client but not sure if related.

maya: Sable confirmed the 401s were a bad client key rotation; they fixed that ~15m before the spike. the 429s are post-fix and persist.

sophie: quick mitigation options:
- bump min_replicas to 4 for d-sable-4 (fast)
- temporarily increase burst refill_rate for their account (account ops)
- enable prewarm for the pool to avoid placement latency
- add a temporary admission policy to favor smaller responses (reduce max_tokens)

liam: agreed. i'll handle changing min_replicas and prewarm. @ops-bot can you run the change with the dry-run then apply?

ops-bot: request received: apply pool config change d-sable-4 -> min_replicas=4 prewarm=true. dry-run success. applying now...

ops-bot: change applied. new current_replicas=4. autoscaler cooldown reset.

maya: Sable reports 429s dropped to near-zero within ~90s of the change and average latency improved to ~110ms. they still see occasional 503s from single nodes (noisy GPU).

diego: opened a noisy-neighbor ticket for node=gpu-12 to eviction queue. I also bumped their temporary burst refill to 3000_tokens_per_minute for 2 hours to let them catch up; billing notified.

noah: important to capture why burst credits were drained so fast: their traffic pattern is small requests with high token expansion (many tokens per request). our headroom calc uses median token count, not worst-case; need to revisit or add percentile guard.

liam: repro steps we used locally to recreate the failure:
1) run a load generator with a 60s ramp to 5k tps hitting /v1/generate with model redwood-7b and max_tokens=512
2) watch admission metrics: admission.rejections{reason=burst_credits_exhausted} spikes when burst_credits hits 0
3) simulate one noisy GPU by limiting perf on a single replica to force queueing.

sophie: test command (example):
```
hey -n 60000 -c 400 -q 0.01 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -m POST -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","prompt":"short","max_tokens":512}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

liam: follow-ups:
- [P0] adjust min_replicas and enable prewarm permanently for d-sable-4 while they shard traffic (assigned: liam)
- [P1] add a headroom calc tweak to use 95th percentile token usage in admission budget (assigned: noah)
- [P1] audit burst credit refill math for accounts with many small high-token requests (assigned: diego)
- [P2] schedule a noisy-neighbor mitigation to improve placement/eviction logic (assigned: eng-infra)

maya: Sable praised the fast triage. they're asking for a short postmortem and an ETA on the headroom change.

noah: ETA for headroom change is 3 business days to design + 5 days to roll with canaries. will draft a proposal tomorrow.

diego: billing has applied the temporary refill and will invoice as a one-off credit adjustment. tracking id BILL-2468.

sophie: I'll create the postmortem doc and run the repro harness in staging to validate the 95th percentile headroom change.

liam: closing loop for this thread: immediate mitigation succeeded, customer back to normal TPS, moving to postmortem and policy changes.

maya: thanks all. I'll DM Sable the interim notes and post the postmortem link here when it's ready. :thumbsup:
